description.x: Pupils practise taking a local issue apart, in teams.

techniques.x: Jigsaw group work, issue analysis, class discussion.

objective.x: To teach pupils to read a newspaper report critically. They will learn about their own town on the way.

materials.x: Three newspaper reports on one local argument connected to sustainability. They should not all take the same side.

sequence.x: Split the class into teams of three.
Give each member of a team a different one of the three reports. Each pupil reads their own report twice, in silence.

Now regroup. Everyone who read report one sits together, everyone who read report two, and so on. In these groups they work out the main points of their report and rehearse how they will explain it. Then the groups break up and the original teams of three come back together.
Each pupil explains their report to their team. The other two ask questions until they understand it.
Each team writes answers to four questions.
What is the argument about, and what has it to do with sustainability?
What is being assumed without being said?
Where is the reader being pushed?
Then lead a class discussion, taking something from every team.

closure.x: What did you learn today about newspapers as a source of information?

evaluation.x: Listen to the answers to the four questions, and to the closing one. They tell you a great deal about what has landed.

extension.x: Run it again on a different argument. The repetition is what turns this into a skill rather than a lesson.

safety.x: Pupils move around during this. Chairs stay where they are, and nobody gets shoved.

source.x: Clark, P. 2000. Teaching Controversial Issues, Green Teacher, Vol. 62.
Jigsaw Classroom. Jigsaw in 10 easy steps. http://www.jigsaw.org/steps.htm (Accessed July 1, 2010.)
